title: Retry Patterns
description: Learn retry patterns for handling transient failures in microservices communication.

data.text: Retry patterns automatically retry failed operations, handling transient failures like network blips and temporary service unavailability. Amazon, Google, and Netflix all use sophisticated retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter.

Retry only for idempotent operations or when you are certain the operation has not been processed. Never retry non-idempotent operations like payment charges without careful consideration, as you may create duplicates.

data.title: Common Retry Strategies
items: Immediate retry: Retry once immediately (for network timeouts only)
Linear backoff: Wait fixed intervals between retries
Exponential backoff: Double the wait time after each failure
Exponential backoff with jitter: Add randomness to prevent thundering herd

data.title: Thundering Herd Problem
data.text: If many clients retry at the same time after a failure, they can overwhelm the recovering service. Exponential backoff with jitter spreads retries over time, preventing this problem.

items.question: How many times should I retry?
items.answer: 3-5 retries is typical. More retries increase latency and load. Use a circuit breaker alongside retries to prevent overwhelming a failing service.

items.question: What errors should I retry?
items.answer: Retry 408 (timeout), 429 (rate limit), 502 (bad gateway), 503 (service unavailable), and 504 (gateway timeout). Do not retry 400 (bad request) or 404 (not found).

items.question: Should I retry inside the gateway?
items.answer: Yes, but also retry inside services for internal calls. Gateway retries protect clients; service retries protect internal communication.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Retry only idempotent or safe-to-retry operations
Use exponential backoff with jitter to prevent thundering herd
Combine with circuit breakers for resilience
data.takeaway: Retries handle transient failures gracefully, but must be used carefully to avoid making problems worse.
